note_on_method: One filter slug has a lawful data driver in Tallahassee. Outdoor does, because the City's pickleball page sorts its venues into an indoor section and an outdoor section and every published count sits in the outdoor one, or is split by the City's own words at Jake Gaither. Free has two venues, LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, where the City schedules Open Play and writes that it is free - one short of a page. Lights has one, Walker-Ford's "night play is available". Indoor has one, Jake Gaither's single court. Public has none anywhere on this site.

slots.why_this_filter: All seven Tallahassee venues hold outdoor pickleball courts and thirty-three of the city's thirty-four verified courts are outdoors, so this page is nearly the whole city, and it is worth saying plainly why it exists. The City draws the line itself. Its pickleball page has two sections, "Indoor Pickleball Courts & Schedules" and "Outdoor Pickleball Courts & Schedules", and every published count sits in the second - or, at Jake Gaither, is split by the City's own words, "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts". This site publishes an indoor-or-outdoor answer only when an operator states one, and Tallahassee states it for every court it counts. The practical reason to filter is that outdoors is where the City's first-come rule lives. "All Outdoor Courts are First-Come First-Play except during the times noted below", the page says, and "Indoor courts do not have First-Come First-Play available" - so an outdoor court in Tallahassee is one you can walk onto whenever nothing is scheduled, with a 90-minute limit when others are waiting, and an indoor court is one you book or join at a session. The outdoor timetable is also where the free play is: Open Play at LeVerne Payne on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday and at Tom Brown on Monday, Wednesday and Sunday, drop-in and free in the City's words, run under the "RACK" rotation with games to 11, or to 9 when six are waiting. Reserved Play at Tom Brown and Winthrop costs $3.50 to $5.75 a session and can be booked online. Lighting is stated at one outdoor venue, Walker-Ford's "night play is available"; hours at one, Jake Gaither's 8:00am-9:00pm; surface at none. The largest outdoor set is Tom Brown's twelve.
slots.what_qualifies: A venue appears here when the City of Tallahassee's pickleball page lists it under "Outdoor Pickleball Courts & Schedules" with a court count, and this site records that count as outdoor courts. Seven qualify: Tom Brown Park with twelve, LeVerne Payne Community Center and Winthrop Park with six each, Walker-Ford Community Center with three, and Jake Gaither Community Center, Jack L. McLean Jr. Community Center and Lafayette Park with two each. Three need a word. Jake Gaither qualifies on its two outdoor courts and carries an indoor court as well, on the City's split "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts"; the indoor one does not count here. McLean qualifies on a stated count of two although the City prints a resurfacing notice beside it saying the courts are unavailable "until december 5, 2025" - the count stands, the notice is printed on the venue page as the City prints it, and the build fails on the day the City removes it. Tom Brown qualifies on twelve that are two kinds, four standalone and eight on "tennis courts 1-4", which the City counts as pickleball courts and so does this site. What does not qualify is Four Oaks Park, six courts "used for pickleball only" with an Open Play and Reserved Play schedule to 10:00pm, not published at all because "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard" is found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap; and the four community centres on the City's indoor list with sessions and no count - Lawrence-Gregory, Lincoln, Sue Herndon McCollum and the Tallahassee Senior Center - which would not belong on an outdoor page in any case.

faqs.q: Which outdoor courts in Tallahassee have lights?
faqs.a: The City states one: Walker-Ford Community Center, "3 courts - night play is available". No other outdoor venue carries a lighting statement, so the rest are recorded as unverified, and Tallahassee has no lights page.

LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, during their Open Play sessions, which the City writes are "drop-in and free". The other five venues are first come, first play with no stated price, so they carry no fee answer.

faqs.q: Which outdoor venues state their hours?
faqs.a: One. Jake Gaither's line reads "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday". The other six carry a weekly session grid or a first-come note, but no opening or closing time.

faqs.q: Why is Four Oaks Park not here, with six courts?
faqs.a: Because "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard" is found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap, and a venue at an address nobody can locate does not publish. Its six courts are "used for pickleball only" and scheduled seven days a week.

faqs.q: Can I reserve an outdoor court?
faqs.a: Only for Reserved Play sessions, at Tom Brown Park and Winthrop Park, online through Court Reserve or on 850-891-4940. Open Play is drop-in and first-come hours are not booked.

sources.evidence: The seven published addresses matched at house-number level and were placed in Leon County, FL, inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city - five through the Census address file as the City writes them, and two (Tom Brown Park, "501 EASTERWOOD DR"; Lafayette Park, "501 INGLESIDE AVE") on Census answers that change the City's street type where OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the City's spelling. "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard" (Four Oaks Park, 6 courts) is found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap, which is why that venue does not appear on this page.
